survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Lithuania using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the weighting implementation details are not recoverable from this document alone. Analysts using the OECD PISA database should follow the PISA technical documentation for weight and variance estimation procedures when reproducing these estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive results factsheet that reports proficiency levels, mean performance trends, and subgroup comparisons rather than training or evaluating predictive models. As such, it does not provide an explicit methodological section describing how plausible values (PVs) and missing data were handled for any statistical modeling pipeline. The factsheet therefore does not report PV-combining rules or missing-data procedures, which are typically detailed in the PISA technical documentation and main report rather than in the country factsheet.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample reported for Lithuania consists of 7,257 students in 292 schools who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science. The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond PISA’s standard data quality and technical standards; it states that, for Lithuania, all data met PISA quality standards and were considered fit for reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Lithuania factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Lithuania performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results relate to trends since 2006 and to subgroup patterns within Lithuania. PISA 2022 used two two-hour subject tests with rotated booklets, so different students received different item sets and subject combinations; students also completed a background questionnaire and school principals completed a school questionnaire. The factsheet reports mean performance comparisons to the OECD average, proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender. It also highlights COVID-19-related learning disruptions and students’ well-being and classroom experiences. The document is descriptive and does not provide an ML modeling pipeline, PV-handling specification, or missing-data procedure details; those are typically covered in the PISA technical documentation and main report.
